subject: Clarifying PO fields, advance slab triggers, and invoice batching for year-one discount
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@healthsys.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@healthsys.com
Date: 2027-07-25T09:12:00Z
Subject: PO-format & invoice cadence for Redwood discount

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team liked the latency profiles. Procurement surfaced two items they need clarified before we can proceed with the signed PO and the initial billing:

- Exact PO fields required on the header (our ERP needs a specific PO number format and GL/BU mapping).
- Whether Redwood can issue consolidated monthly invoices vs. weekly invoices for separate business units.
- Confirmation of the net terms that apply to the promotional discount you quoted (you mentioned Net30 subject to PO).

We are discussing an advance slab (an up-front partial prepayment tied to a runway discount) on our side, but our finance team insists the vendor invoice must include: vendor remit address, tax ID, and the customer PO number on each invoice line. Can you send a sample invoice or the PO template you require?

Thanks,
Ellen Park
Sr. Procurement Manager
HealthSys Inc.

Attachment: none

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@healthsys.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-25T12:08:00Z
Subject: Re: PO-format & invoice cadence for Redwood discount

Ellen — really appreciate the clear list. Quick answers and next steps below; attaching our PO template so you can forward to your ERP team.

1) PO fields: we require PO number, billing entity (we accept either Redwood Inference, Inc. or Redwood Inference, LLC depending on your AP setup), remit-to (we include both ACH and wire instructions), and optional BU/GL tag in the PO memo. If your ERP needs a specific PO number pattern, we can accept that as long as the PO number is included on each invoice line.

2) Invoice cadence: standard is monthly consolidated invoices by default. We can support weekly invoices by BU but that typically increases our billing ops overhead. For the year-one promotional discount you referenced, the discount is tied to an annual committed spend and requires consolidated monthly invoicing (so we can reconcile usage against the commit). If you need weekly splits, we can still apply the discount but the credit reconciliation will be done monthly.

3) Net terms: promotional pricing is Net30 from invoice date. If HealthSys needs Net45 or Net60, we can consider that but it will reduce the up-front discount by ~1.5% for Net45 and ~3% for Net60 (finance requirement). We can include Net45 for an additional approval step on our side.

Attached: PO_template_v2.pdf (application/pdf) — contains the exact header fields and sample invoice layout.

Next step: Monica (cc'd) will follow up with a short reconciliation note for the advance slab — we want to ensure the prepayment is applied as a credit against monthly consolidated invoices and is reflected on the first invoice.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@healthsys.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-26T16:22:00Z
Subject: Re: PO-format & invoice cadence for Redwood discount

Hi Ellen — looping in Marissa from Finance for the accounting specifics. A couple of clarifications from our side to avoid surprises:

• If HealthSys sends an advance slab (prepayment), we will issue a credit memo applied to the first monthly consolidated invoice after the prepayment posts. The credit memo will include the PO number provided at the time of prepayment.
• For GL mapping: we can put a per-line memo field that contains your BU code; however, the invoice total must still show the official PO number on the invoice header and each invoice line for your ERP to ingest.
• For tax and remit: our invoices always include tax ID and remit-to; we can add a separate 'payment instructions' PDF as part of the billing bundle if your AP needs additional details.

Marissa — can you confirm how the discount will be reflected on the invoice (line-item percent vs. separate credit line)? We want to be explicit for HealthSys so their AR team can automate processing.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Revenue Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@healthsys.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-27T15:40:00Z
Subject: Re: PO-format & invoice cadence for Redwood discount

Ellen — quick finance confirmation.

- Discount treatment: for the promotional year-one discount tied to the committed spend, we'll show the discount as a separate credit line on the monthly consolidated invoice ("Year-One Commit Credit") and then show net charges below. Reason: keeps your line-item usage intact for reconciling usage and maps cleanly to our accounting and revenue recognition for credits/deferrals.
- If HealthSys needs the percent shown inline per SKU/line, we can do that but we'd need to reconcile a secondary credit memo for any adjustments at month-end. Slight preference is separate credit line to minimize reconciliation errors.
- Net terms: as Karthik noted, Net30 by default; if you require Net45 we will build that into the SOW and adjust the discount schedule accordingly.

I'll also upload a PDF sample invoice showing the credit line format. Attaching Redwood_SOW_v3.docx with the clause language we propose for invoicing and the commit/credit mechanics.

Marissa Cole
Director, Finance (Billing)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_SOW_v3.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)
